prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: Back at it! #KeepClimbing  https://t.co/tTSY0B8yPw
Delta: Hi Alan, Great picture!  Glad to have you flying with us today! :-)  Thank you for your loyalty.   *HML

Customer: big thanks and shout out to your ATL customer service associate  Steve Tillman.  He gave me a great bday gift and got me home early!!
Delta: Thanks for the shout out, Birthday Girl! We're so happy you've chosen us for your travels! :-) *AAB

Customer: I can’t give my wife her gift if you guys don’t put my bag on the plane. #happywifehappylife
Delta: ...airport?  *HSD 2/2

Customer: 🛫 X #KeepClimbing X #Seattle X seahawks  X  🎥🎞🎥 is on the move X… https://t.co/ELc5qHUR4o
Delta: Nice to have you on board. Have a great flight:-) *HPL

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: praise):
"""Big thanks to  for surprising my wife with a gift bag  for completing her doctorate! Another reason to #keepclimbing https://t.co/KeFFsB16uH"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Congrats to your wife on her doctorate! We’re thrilled she enjoyed the surprise gift bag. Thanks for sharing your celebration with us! :-)
